result.title: Lifelong Context Adaptation through Bidirectional Memory-Skill Learning
result.comment: 42 pages, including references and appendices. 18 figures, 13 tables
result.summary: Lifelong LLM agents must learn from an expanding history of interactions while making each decision within a bounded context window. Memory makes past experience available, but the agent may still need to infer how to solve each new task from the retrieved records. Skills provide reusable procedures, yet may omit the task-specific facts needed to apply them. Because retrieved memory and skills shape the agent's behavior, they also influence the experience available for future learning. We introduce MemCryst, a framework for lifelong context adaptation through bidirectional learning of memory and skills with a frozen language model. Recurring episodes stored in memory support skill creation and revision, and the interactions guided by those skills supply new memory for subsequent learning. Facts retrieved from memory and learned skills jointly form the agent's context, while task outcomes adjust the future retrieval influence of the records actually served without rewriting their content. Across ten settings spanning embodied control, long-document reading, conversation, mathematics, and code, MemCryst leads seven reported comparisons. On ALFWorld, joint serving achieves 63.17% success, compared with 59.83% for memory-only and 50.50% for skill-only serving. Code is available at https://github.com/tianyi0216/Memcryst.git

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MemCryst：在冻结语言模型上，让记忆中的重复片段驱动技能创建与修订，技能引导的交互又回写为新记忆，形成记忆—技能双向学习，并用任务结果调整已检索记录的未来检索影响力，在十类任务上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「不重写内容、仅按任务结果调整检索影响力」的做法，可供核查是否能类比 LVR 中的证据筛选、贡献分配与轨迹监督；但研究的是纯文本智能体记忆，未涉及 latent 状态或视觉推理。
